Swept 2026-08-16 with tools/check_api_arity.py, committed alongside this closure.

RESULT over the 460 method declarations in inc/Api.h:
  326  every shared parameter slot agrees
   38  C++ has extra trailing defaulted parameters, shared slots agree -- benign
        by design (the script simply does not expose an option)
    2  MISALIGNED
   94  no C++ declaration the tool could match, so NOT CHECKED

The two misalignments:
  inc-xkd  FindOpenAreas -- slot 2 is Flags to the script and regID to the C++.
           Live, and already filed.
  new      SetGlyphAt -- a 32-bit Glyph declared 16 bits wide in the API and
           cast down in the generated call. Not live; no script calls it.

WHAT THE DISCRIMINATOR TURNED OUT TO BE, because the first three attempts were
useless. Counting parameters flags 45 methods, nearly all benign: a C++ method
may carry trailing defaulted parameters the script does not expose, and
MoveDepth(NewDepth) against MoveDepth(NewDepth, safe=false) is correct. Comparing
parameter NAMES flags 61, nearly all pure renames -- 'fl' against 'flags', 'att'
against 'at'. What actually separates a defect from house style is the TYPE
CLASS of each slot: FindOpenAreas is dangerous because slot 2 is an integer to
the script and an rID to the C++, and the compiler cannot tell those apart
because rID is a uint32 underneath.

THE HONEST LIMIT: 94 of 460, about a fifth, were not checked because the tool
could not find a C++ declaration to compare against. That is a coverage gap, not
a clean bill of health. It is printed in the summary every run, and
'tools/check_api_arity.py --all' lists them.

Fixed. Monster::MoveTowards now asks Door::isPassable() (inc/Feature.h) instead of testing DF_OPEN, so a monster never calls OpenDoor on a broken doorway. Traced the whole chain first: Throw(EV_OPEN) hits the DF_BROKEN arm of Door::Event (src/Feature.cpp:423-434), which answers and returns ABORT without spending time; Monster::OpenDoor reads that zero Timeout as 'the attempt did not happen' and falls through to TryToDestroyThing, so the monster attacked the empty doorway up to five times, one turn each. Worse than this bead first said, which claimed only a wasted turn on the open attempt. src/Player.cpp:494 was examined and deliberately left alone: it asks 'is it open, so should I close it?', which is a different question, and both arms already print a correct message and cost no time on a broken door. Guarded by tools/check_broken_door.sh. Marked upstream: at the fix site and rowed in docs/REPORTING-GATE.md.

Fixed, and it was the source of inc-8zu. Measured with a new gated probe (INCURSION_DOOR_PROBE, src/Feature.cpp): seed 7 through tools/keys/dive12.keys, 3029 Door::SetImage calls over 446 doors. SetImage runs during level generation, before the walls beside a door exist, so ordinary doors were branded DF_BROKEN and kept the brand forever. Before: 42 redraws found a door still branded whose doorframe was readable again, 6 doors ended the level closed and branded broken, and 14 of the 63 brand events hit a LOCKED door -- so a locked door became a walkable hole. After: 0 and 0. Fix: clear the brand on any redraw that can read the frame. Safe because of an invariant the tree keeps -- only two places set DF_BROKEN (this branch alone, and the damage path which sets DF_OPEN|DF_BROKEN together at src/Feature.cpp:655) and only two clear DF_OPEN (the constructor, before any door can break, and EV_CLOSE, which refuses a broken door first), so DF_BROKEN without DF_OPEN can only be this branch's own mark. An occupied doorway is exempt: turning the square solid under a creature would bury it in a wall. The same arm now also restores Flags |= F_SOLID, which nothing put back when a door stopped being passable. Guarded by tools/check_broken_door.sh, which was proved to fail on a build with the fix removed (42 stale, 6 ended). Brian's live save is measured too: his three temple doors at (42,40) (48,37) (54,40) carry flags 0x40 and stand in readable horizontal doorframes (W and E solid), so once anything redraws them they become ordinary closed doors and travel out will refuse until he opens one. Until then the reader fix (inc-8zu) carries the save.
